angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 517,782 km at 118.46 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.4414 +/- 0.0127 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 118.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.744261 +/- 0.111278 solar radii from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract): 517,782 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.69563 +/- 0.069563 solar masses from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4356.47 +/- 196.73 K from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-130 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-130.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.537, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
